segments.text:
By this circumſtance the power of God did ſhine forth more manifeſtly in ſauing Daniel, becauſe they were ſtraightway torne in péeces of the Lyons which had wickedly accuſed him. But if any man ſhould ſay that the Lyons
were full, or that there was ſome other cauſe why Daniel was not torne in peeces: wherfore then, whē he was drawē forth, were the beaſtes ſtraightwayes ſo mad that they did teare & deuoure, not onely one man, but a great cōpany? Of many nobles, none eſcapeth ſafe. Then are their wiues like wiſe caſt into them, and alſo their children: but the Lyons could ſcarce be able to deuoure ſo many, & yet euery one of them periſh both great & ſmall. How then eſcaped Daniel? We ſée that God by this compariſon would make manifeſt his power, leſt any man ſhould obiect that Daniel was forſaken of the Lyons becauſe they were now ful, & did not deſire the pray: For then they would haue bene cōtented with thrée or foure men: but now they deuoure both men, womē and children. Hereby then it appeareth that the mouthes of the Lyons were bridled by God, ſeing that Daniel was ſafe a whole night, and they were killed as ſoone as they were caſt into the denne: becauſe we ſée agayne that the beaſtes were driuen to a ſodayne rage that they did not tary till they came to the grounde, but did teare them as they were fallyng.
